sentences.text: Shri Dharmendra Kumar Kaurab - Advocate for appellant  No.2849/2024.

Shri Sandeep Shukla - Advocate for respondent-CBI.
I.A. No.5774/2024 on behalf of appellant-Ashish Sharma, I.A.No.5483/2024 on behalf of appellant Vasudev Tyagi, I.A.No.5764/2024 on behalf of appellant-Mukesh Kumar Rawat, I.A. No.6655/2024 on behalf of appellant-Sunil Kr Tyagi, I.A. No.5767/2024 on behalf of appellant-Azab Singh Kushwah and I.A.No.5766/2024 on behalf of appellants-Awdhesh Goswami and Sunil Shrivastava have been filed for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Appellants Ashish Sharma, Vasudev Tyagi, Mukesh Kumar Rawat, Sunil Kr Tyagi, Azab Singh Kushwah, Awdhesh Goswami and Sunil Shrivastava have been convicted for offence under Section 419 r/w 120B of IPC and sentenced to undergo 2 years RI & fine of Rs.1000/-, 420 r/w 120B of IPC and sentenced to undergo 2 years RI & fine of Rs.1000/-, 467 r/w 120B of IPC and sentenced to undergo 7 years RI & fine of Rs.3000/-, 468 r/w 120B of IPC and sentenced to undergo 7 years RI &
fine of Rs.1000/-, 471 r/w 120B of IPC and sentenced to undergo 7 years RI & fine of Rs.3000/- and Section 3(d)(2) r/w 4 of MP Recognized Examination Act 1937 and sentenced to undergo 2 years RI and fine of Rs.1000/- with default stipulations.
Counsel for appellants submitted that no offence under Section 467, 468 of IPC is made out against the appellants as document which is said to be forged was not valuable security.
At best, offence against the appellants may be under Section 465 & 471 of IPC.
For committing offences under Section 419, 420 of IPC, appellants have been sentenced to 2 years RI and fine.
It is submitted that offence under Section 3(d)(2) r/w Section 4 of MP Recognized Examination Act 1937 is punishable with imprisonment of 2 years RI.
On these grounds, counsel for appellants prayed for grant of bail.

sentences.text: Mr. Sandeep Shukla, learned counsel appearing for respondent-CBI opposed the applications filed by appellants for suspension of sentence and it is submitted by him that admission cards and OMR mark-sheets were forged, which are valuable security, therefore, it cannot be said that offence will not fall within definition of under Section 467 & 468 of IPC.
On these grounds, he made a prayer for rejection of applications for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellants.
Heard learned counsel for appellants as well as counsel for respondent.
A t this stage, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, appellants are convicted for a fixed term of sentence, OMR mark-sheet and admission card cannot be said to be a valuable security.
Appellants may be guilty of offence but not for offence under Sections 467, 468 of IPC.

Considering the same and looking to the period of sentence, applications (I.A. No.5774/2024, I.A.
No.5483/2024, I.A. No.5764/2024, I.A. No.5767/2024, I.A. No.6655/2024 and I.A. No.5766/2024)
for suspension of sentence are allowed, subject to depositing fine amount as per the judgment of trial Court, if not already deposited.

It is hereby directed that the custodial sentence awarded to the appellants-Ashish Sharma, Vasudev Tyagi, Mukesh Kumar Rawat, Sunil Kr Tyagi, Azab Singh Kushwah, Awdhesh Goswami and Sunil Shrivastava shall remain suspended during the pendency of these appeals and they shall be released on bail on their furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) each with one solvent surety each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for their appearance before the Registry on 22.05.2024 and on other dates as may be fixed in this regard till final disposal of this appeal.
C.C.
as per rules.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE sp/-
